"""Dev helper (not committed): apply one stage, print each statement's outcome."""

import re
import sys

from risk_copilot.config import load_settings
from risk_copilot.pipeline.deploy import Deployer, split_statements
from risk_copilot.session import open_session

stage = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "procedures"
only = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else ""
s = load_settings(profile="dev")
d = Deployer(s)
bad = 0
with open_session(s) as ss:
    for f in d.stage_files(stage):
        if only and only not in f.name:
            continue
        for st in split_statements(d.render(f)):
            head = " ".join(st.split())[:70]
            try:
                ss.sql(st).collect()
                print("OK ", f.name, head)
            except Exception as e:
                bad += 1
                msg = str(e)
                print("ERR", f.name, msg[:1200])
                body = st[st.find("$$") + 2 :] if "$$" in st else st
                lines = body.splitlines()
                for m in sorted({int(x) for x in re.findall(r"line (\d+)", msg)})[:6]:
                    print(f"  L{m}:", lines[m - 1] if 0 < m <= len(lines) else "?")
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

"""Dev helper (not committed): run SQL statements (separated by a line ';;') from stdin."""

import json
import sys

from risk_copilot.config import load_settings
from risk_copilot.session import open_session

with open_session(s) as ss:
    for q in [p.strip() for p in text.split("\n;;") if p.strip()]:

            continue
        for r in rows[:40]:
            d = r.as_dict()
            print("  ", json.dumps(d, default=str)[:1800])
        if len(rows) > 40:
            print(f"   ... {len(rows)} rows")

"""The case tools (sql/procedures): offline rendering and the invariants REVIEW_STR relies on."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from risk_copilot.config import load_settings
from risk_copilot.pipeline.deploy import Deployer, split_statements


def _rendered(repo_root: Path, profile: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    d = Deployer(load_settings(repo_root=repo_root, profile=profile))
    return {f.name: d.render(f) for f in d.stage_files("procedures")}


@pytest.mark.parametrize("profile", ["dev", "demo"])
def test_procedures_stage_renders_one_object_per_statement(repo_root: Path, profile: str) -> None:
    files = _rendered(repo_root, profile)
    assert sorted(files) == [
        "01_case_tools_common.sql",
        "02_gather_evidence.sql",
        "03_draft_str.sql",
    ]
    assert [len(split_statements(s)) for s in files.values()] == [3, 1, 1]


def test_tool_names_carry_the_profile_suffix(repo_root: Path) -> None:
    dev = _rendered(repo_root, "dev")
    assert "PROCEDURE RISK_COPILOT_DEV.EVIDENCE_CHAIN.GATHER_EVIDENCE_DEV(" in dev["02_gather_evidence.sql"]
    assert "PROCEDURE RISK_COPILOT_DEV.EVIDENCE_CHAIN.DRAFT_STR_DEV(" in dev["03_draft_str.sql"]
    # DRAFT_STR calls the same profile's gatherer, not another profile's.
    assert "CALL RISK_COPILOT_DEV.EVIDENCE_CHAIN.GATHER_EVIDENCE_DEV(" in dev["03_draft_str.sql"]
    demo = _rendered(repo_root, "demo")
    assert "PROCEDURE RISK_COPILOT.EVIDENCE_CHAIN.GATHER_EVIDENCE(" in demo["02_gather_evidence.sql"]


def _logged_queries(sql: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The query texts GATHER_EVIDENCE stores, unescaped from their DEFAULT literals."""
    found = re.findall(r"(q_\w+) VARCHAR DEFAULT '(.*?)';\n", sql, flags=re.S)
    return {name: text.replace("''", "'") for name, text in found}


def test_every_logged_query_takes_exactly_one_bind(repo_root: Path) -> None:
    # REVIEW_STR re-runs a log as EXECUTE IMMEDIATE <sql_text> USING (<params[0]>).
    queries = _logged_queries(_rendered(repo_root, "dev")["02_gather_evidence.sql"])
    assert sorted(queries) == ["q_clauses", "q_deposits", "q_party", "q_summary"]
    for name, text in queries.items():
        assert text.count("?") == 1, name
        assert ";" not in text, name


def test_logged_queries_are_fully_qualified(repo_root: Path) -> None:
    # A log is re-run long after deploy, from any schema: no relative names.
    queries = _logged_queries(_rendered(repo_root, "dev")["02_gather_evidence.sql"])
    for name, text in queries.items():
        for table in re.findall(r"\b(?:FROM|JOIN)\s+([A-Z_][\w.]*)", text):
            if table in {"p", "ids", "d", "r", "span"}:
                continue
            assert table.startswith("RISK_COPILOT_DEV."), (name, table)


def test_the_clause_list_includes_the_filing_duties(repo_root: Path) -> None:
    q = _logged_queries(_rendered(repo_root, "dev")["02_gather_evidence.sql"])["q_clauses"]
    assert "'STR_FILING_SLA_DAYS'" in q and "'PRINCIPAL_OFFICER_ATTESTATION_REQUIRED'" in q


def test_the_narrative_template_holds_no_figure(repo_root: Path) -> None:
    common = _rendered(repo_root, "dev")["01_case_tools_common.sql"]
    (template,) = re.findall(r"'narrative_template', '(.*?)'\n", common)
    assert re.findall(r"\{([a-z_]+)\}", template)
    assert not re.search(r"\d", template), "a number in the template would bypass computed_values"


def test_draft_records_the_configured_narrative_author(repo_root: Path) -> None:
    draft = _rendered(repo_root, "dev")["03_draft_str.sql"]
    assert "'TEMPLATE_V1'" in draft
    assert "FIU_IND_STR" in draft

def call(proc: str, *args: Any) -> Any:
    """CALL a procedure; returns its scalar result and drops cached reads."""
    marks = ", ".join("?" for _ in args)
    rows = session().sql(f"CALL {proc}({marks})", params=list(args)).collect()
    st.cache_data.clear()
    return rows[0][0] if rows else None

# ---- the STR workflow ------------------------------------------------------ #


def case_artifacts(case_id: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Every STR version for a case, newest first, with its latest review."""
    return cached(
        f"""
        SELECT a.artifact_id, a.version, a.status, a.validation_status, a.content_hash,
               a.created_at, f.finding_id, f.author_model, f.prompt_version,
               r.decision AS review_decision, r.review_id, r.defects_found, r.checks_run,
               r.numeric_recompute_passed, r.citation_resolution_passed,
               r.clause_in_effect_passed, r.reviewed_at
        FROM {EV}.ARTIFACT a
        JOIN {EV}.FINDING f ON f.finding_id = a.finding_id
        LEFT JOIN {EV}.REVIEW r ON r.finding_id = a.finding_id
        WHERE f.case_id = ?
        QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY a.artifact_id
                                   ORDER BY r.reviewed_at DESC NULLS LAST) = 1
        ORDER BY a.version DESC
        """,
        (case_id,),
    )


def artifact(artifact_id: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    df = cached(
        f"""
        SELECT a.*, f.case_id, f.computed_values, f.cited_clause_ids, f.author_model,
               f.prompt_version, f.version AS finding_version
        FROM {EV}.ARTIFACT a JOIN {EV}.FINDING f ON f.finding_id = a.finding_id
        WHERE a.artifact_id = ?
        """,
        (artifact_id,),
    )
    return None if df.empty else df.iloc[0].to_dict()


def evidence_rows(case_id: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return cached(
        f"""
        SELECT ref_type, ref_id, materiality, ref_table, as_of_ts, evidence_id
        FROM {EV}.EVIDENCE WHERE case_id = ? ORDER BY ref_type, ref_id
        """,
        (case_id,),
    )


def query_logs(case_id: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return cached(
        f"""
        SELECT q.bind_values:name::STRING AS query, q.query_log_id, q.result_row_count AS rows,
               q.result_hash, q.canonical_form_version AS form, q.executed_at, q.execution_ms,
               q.sql_text
        FROM {EV}.EVIDENCE_QUERY_LOG q JOIN {EV}.EVIDENCE e ON e.evidence_id = q.evidence_id
        WHERE e.case_id = ? ORDER BY q.executed_at, q.query_log_id
        """,
        (case_id,),
    )


def signoff_queue() -> pd.DataFrame:
    """STRs the Reviewer approved and no officer has signed yet."""
    return cached(
        f"""
        SELECT a.artifact_id, f.case_id, p.full_name, c.branch_region, a.version,
               c.sla_deadline, a.created_at
        FROM {EV}.ARTIFACT a
        JOIN {EV}.FINDING f ON f.finding_id = a.finding_id
        JOIN {EV}.CASE_RECORD c ON c.case_id = f.case_id
        LEFT JOIN {DT['dim_party']} p ON p.party_id = c.party_id
        WHERE a.status = 'REVIEWED'
        ORDER BY c.sla_deadline, a.created_at
        """
    )


def attestations() -> pd.DataFrame:
    return cached(
        f"""
        SELECT t.attested_at, t.decision, t.attestor, t.attestor_role, f.case_id, t.artifact_id,
               a.status AS artifact_status, t.attested_content_hash = a.content_hash AS hash_matches,
               t.comment
        FROM {EV}.ATTESTATION t
        JOIN {EV}.ARTIFACT a ON a.artifact_id = t.artifact_id
        JOIN {EV}.FINDING f ON f.finding_id = a.finding_id
        ORDER BY t.attested_at DESC
        """
    )


def filing_integrity() -> int:
    """FILED artifacts without a matching, hash-bound attestation. Must be 0."""
    df = cached(
        f"""
        SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM {EV}.ARTIFACT a
        WHERE a.status = 'FILED' AND NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM {EV}.ATTESTATION t
            WHERE t.artifact_id = a.artifact_id AND t.decision = 'ATTESTED'
              AND t.attested_content_hash = a.content_hash)
        """
    )
    return int(df.iloc[0]["n"])

"""Rendering an STR and its review, shared by the case and sign-off pages."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

from lib.db import variant

CHECKS = [
    ("numeric_recompute", "Every figure recomputed from its logged query"),
    ("citation_resolution", "Every cited clause and evidence id resolves"),
    ("clause_in_effect", "Every cited clause was in force on the deposit dates"),
    ("schema", "Required STR fields present; content matches its hash"),
]

STATUS_HELP = {
    "DRAFT": "Drafted, waiting for the Reviewer.",
    "REJECTED": "The Reviewer found defects. Fix by redrafting; it is never edited.",
    "REVIEWED": "The Reviewer approved it. Waiting for the Principal Officer.",
    "FILED": "Attested by the Principal Officer and filed.",
    "RETURNED": "Returned by the Principal Officer for a redraft.",
    "SUPERSEDED": "Replaced by a newer version.",
}


def str_document(a: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """The filing as an officer would read it."""
    content = variant(a["content"]) or {}
    subject = content.get("subject") or {}
    st.markdown(f"**Suspicious Transaction Report** · `{a['artifact_id']}` · version {a['version']}")
    c = st.columns(4)
    c[0].metric("Status", a["status"], help=STATUS_HELP.get(a["status"]))
    c[1].metric("Subject", subject.get("FULL_NAME", "-"))
    c[2].metric("Typology", str(content.get("typology_id", "-")).replace("TYP_", ""))
    c[3].metric("File by", str(content.get("filing_deadline", "-")))
    st.markdown("##### Grounds of suspicion")
    st.info(content.get("grounds_of_suspicion", "-"))

    figures = variant(content.get("computed_values")) or {}
    rows = [
        {
            "placeholder": k,
            "stated as": v.get("display"),
            "source query": v.get("query_log_id"),
            "column": v.get("column"),
        }
        for k, v in sorted(figures.items())
    ]
    with st.expander(f"Where every figure comes from ({len(rows)} figures)"):
        st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame(rows), hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
        st.caption(
            f"Narrative written by `{a.get('author_model')}` from template "
            f"`{a.get('prompt_version')}`; it contains placeholders only. Each figure is "
            "read from a logged, hashed query."
        )
    with st.expander("Cited clauses and transactions"):
        st.write(", ".join(variant(content.get("cited_clause_ids")) or []))
        tx = variant(content.get("transactions")) or []
        if tx:
            st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame(tx), hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
    st.caption(f"content_hash `{a['content_hash']}`")


def review_result(row: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """The Reviewer's checklist and defects for one artifact."""
    if not row.get("review_decision") or pd.isna(row.get("review_decision")):
        st.caption("Not reviewed yet.")
        return
    defects = variant(row.get("defects_found")) or []
    failed = {d.get("check") for d in defects}
    approve = row["review_decision"] == "APPROVE"
    (st.success if approve else st.error)(
        f"Reviewer: **{row['review_decision']}**"
        + ("" if approve else f" -- {len(defects)} defect(s) found")
    )
    for key, label in CHECKS:
        mark = ":red[FAIL]" if key in failed else ":green[PASS]"
        st.markdown(f"{mark}   {label}")
    for d in defects:
        st.markdown(f"- **{d.get('check')}**: {d.get('message')}")
    checks = variant(row.get("checks_run")) or {}
    if checks:
        st.caption(
            f"{checks.get('queries_recomputed')} queries re-run, "
            f"{checks.get('figures_checked')} figures, {checks.get('clauses_checked')} clauses, "
            f"{checks.get('evidence_checked')} evidence ids checked. No model involved."
        )

"""Principal Officer sign-off: the human gate. Nothing is filed without it."""

import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st
from lib import data
from lib.db import PROC, call, reason
from lib.str_view import review_result, str_document

st.title("Principal Officer sign-off")
st.caption(
    "PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, Rule 7: the Principal Officer bears the filing "
    "obligation. The system cannot file on its own -- ATTEST_STR refuses unless the caller holds "
    "the compliance officer role, the Reviewer approved, and this exact version is unchanged."
)

queue = data.signoff_queue()
if queue.empty:
    st.info("No STR is awaiting sign-off. Approved drafts appear here.")
else:
    labels = {
        r.artifact_id: f"{r.artifact_id} -- {r.full_name} ({r.branch_region}), file by "
        f"{str(r.sla_deadline)[:10]}"
        for r in queue.itertuples()
    }
    aid = st.selectbox("STR awaiting attestation", list(labels), format_func=labels.get)
    a = data.artifact(aid)
    if a:
        left, right = st.columns([3, 2])
        with left:
            str_document(a)
        with right:
            st.markdown("##### Reviewer's result")
            arts = data.case_artifacts(a["case_id"])
            row = arts[arts["artifact_id"] == aid]
            if not row.empty:
                review_result(row.iloc[0].to_dict())
            st.markdown("##### Your decision")
            with st.form("attest", clear_on_submit=False):
                attestor = st.text_input("Your name", placeholder="Principal Officer")
                decision = st.radio(
                    "Decision",
                    ["ATTESTED", "RETURNED"],
                    format_func={
                        "ATTESTED": "Attest and file",
                        "RETURNED": "Return for redraft",
                    }.get,
                    horizontal=True,
                )
                comment = st.text_area("Comment (optional)")
                confirm = st.checkbox(
                    f"I have read this exact version (hash {a['content_hash'][:12]}…) "
                    "and take responsibility for this decision."
                )
                submitted = st.form_submit_button("Sign", type="primary")
            if submitted:
                if not confirm:
                    st.error("Tick the confirmation to sign.")
                else:
                    try:
                        result = call(PROC["attest_str"], aid, decision, attestor, comment or None)
                        st.session_state["signed"] = result
                        st.rerun()
                    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- the gate's reason, shown verbatim
                        st.error(f"Refused: {reason(exc)}")

signed = st.session_state.pop("signed", None)
if signed:
    st.success(
        f"{signed.get('decision')}: {signed.get('artifact_id')} is now "
        f"{signed.get('artifact_status')}. Attestation {signed.get('attestation_id')} records "
        f"hash {str(signed.get('attested_content_hash'))[:12]}…"
    )

st.subheader("Attestation register")
reg = data.attestations()
if reg.empty:
    st.caption("No attestations yet.")
else:
    st.dataframe(reg, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
bad = data.filing_integrity()
st.metric(
    "Filed STRs without a matching, hash-bound attestation",
    bad,
    help="Must always be 0. Checked live against ARTIFACT and ATTESTATION.",
)
if bad:
    st.error("Integrity breach: an STR is FILED without a matching attestation.")

type_specific_data.fullPageContents:
Cortex Agents
Get started with Cortex AgentsTry it in Snowsight


Overview
Cortex Agents is a fully managed agentic platform for building and running AI agents within Snowflake’s governed environment. An agent reasons over a request, plans the work, calls tools, executes code, and generates a response, without requiring you to build or operate your own orchestration loop, runtime, or sandbox infrastructure. Data access is governed by Snowflake privileges and the execution context of each configured tool.
Agents bring your structured and unstructured data together in a single governed workflow. They generate SQL over structured data using Cortex Analyst semantic views and use Cortex Search to retrieve insights from unstructured sources, then reason over the combined results. You can extend what an agent can do with several types of tools:

A built-in code execution tool that, when enabled, runs Python in a secure, isolated sandbox to process data and perform calculations.
A Data to Chart tool that generates visualizations from data.
Custom tools built from stored procedures and user-defined functions (UDFs) to call backend systems or implement your own business logic.
Packaged agent skills, modular bundles of instructions and scripts that give an agent repeatable, task-specific capabilities.
MCP connectors to remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, letting agents discover and invoke tools hosted by providers such as Atlassian Jira, Salesforce, or your own applications.
Web search for real-time information from the public internet.

Threads maintain conversation context across turns, so your client application doesn’t have to manage state. After deployment, you can monitor agents, collect end-user feedback, and run evaluations to continuously refine their behavior.
To answer a request, an agent follows a reasoning loop with three steps:

Plan: The agent parses the request and decides how to answer it. It can disambiguate a vague question (for example, “Tell me about Acme Supplies” might refer to products, location, or sales personnel), split a complex request into subtasks (for example, “What are the differences between contract terms for Acme Supplies and Acme Stationery?”), and choose which tool to use for each part.
Use tools: The agent calls the tools it selected, such as Cortex Analyst for structured data, Cortex Search for unstructured data, or the code execution tool to process results.
Reflect and respond: The agent evaluates the results from each tool to decide what to do next, whether that’s asking a clarifying question, calling another tool, or generating a final response. This loop lets the agent handle complex, multi-step questions.

The agent repeats this loop as needed within a single request.
You define an agent as a reusable object that bundles its model, tools, and orchestration instructions. Create one in Snowsight, with the Cortex Agents SQL commands, or through the REST API, then integrate it into your application using the REST API. You guide its behavior with natural-language instructions, and you can choose the language model that powers it or let Snowflake select one automatically. In addition to calling agents from your own applications through the REST API, users can interact with them in Snowflake CoWork and Cortex Code.
An agent’s tools give it access to your data. An agent with no tools configured can still
hold a conversation, but it answers only from the language model’s general knowledge and can’t query
anything in your account. If the caller’s role can’t use every configured tool, the run can still
continue with the tools it can access. See Inaccessible tool handling.
To build your first agent end to end, see Get started with Cortex Agents.
For more scenarios, see
Tutorials.
NoteWhile Snowflake strives to provide high-quality responses, the accuracy of the LLM responses or
the citations provided is not guaranteed. You should review all answers from the Agents API before serving them to your users.

Key concepts
Cortex Agents is built around the following concepts:
ConceptDescriptionAgentA schema-level object that bundles the agent’s model, tools, orchestration settings, and instructions. Create it once and reuse it across interactions and applications. Permanent agents persist until dropped; temporary agents last for the current session only. Secure agents hide the specification from non-owner roles.ToolsHow the agent acts on your data and systems: Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search, code execution, custom tools, and more. See Tools.OrchestrationThe LLM-driven plan, use tools, reflect loop the agent runs to answer a request. You shape it with natural-language planning and response instructions.ThreadPersisted conversation context across turns, so your client application doesn’t manage state. Create a thread object and reference its ID in agent interactions.RunA single request to an agent through the agent:run API. The agent emits events throughout the run that surface its reasoning, tool calls, and reflections.ExpandShow lessSee more


Models
When creating an agent, we recommend selecting auto for the model. With this option, Cortex automatically selects the highest quality model for your account, and quality improves as new models become available.
Cortex Agents supports the following models. These models run through cross-region inference, so availability is shown by cross-region routing scope (the value of the CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION account parameter), not by individual region. A model is available to your account when your routing scope is marked for that model. Columns match the scopes listed in Regional availability and Model availability.
ProviderModelStatusCross Cloud (Any Region)AWS Global (Cross-Region)AWS US (Cross-Region)AWS US Commercial Gov (Cross-Region)AWS US FedRAMP High Plus (Cross-Region)AWS US DoD (Cross-Region)AWS EU (Cross-Region)AWS APJ (Cross-Region)AWS AU (Cross-Region)Azure Global (Cross-Region)Azure US (Cross-Region)Azure US FedRAMP High Plus (Cross-Region)Azure EU (Cross-Region)Google Cloud US (Cross-Region)Anthropicclaude-opus-5GA✔✔✔✔✔✔Anthropicclaude-opus-4-8GA✔✔✔✔✔✔Anthropicclaude-opus-4-7GA✔✔✔✔✔✔Anthropicclaude-opus-4-6GA✔✔✔✔✔✔Anthropicclaude-opus-4-5GA✔✔✔✔Anthropicclaude-sonnet-5GA✔✔✔✔✔✔Anthropicclaude-sonnet-4-6GA✔✔✔✔✔✔✔Anthropicclaude-sonnet-4-5GA✔✔✔✔✔✔✔✔✔✔Anthropicclaude-4-sonnet (legacy)GA✔✔✔✔✔✔Anthropicclaude-haiku-4-5GA✔✔✔✔✔✔✔OpenAIopenai-gpt-5.4GA✔✔✔✔OpenAIopenai-gpt-5.2GA✔✔✔OpenAIopenai-gpt-5.1GA✔✔✔✔OpenAIopenai-gpt-5GA✔✔✔✔OpenAIopenai-gpt-5-miniGA✔✔✔OpenAIopenai-gpt-4.1 (legacy)GA✔✔✔Googlegemini-3.1-proPublic preview✔✔Googlegemini-3.5-flashGA✔✔ExpandShow lessSee more
Public preview models aren’t intended for production workloads. After a model’s legacy date, only
accounts that already used the model can continue to call it until end-of-life; accounts that had
not used it can’t start. Run SHOW CORTEX BASE MODELS
to see legacy and end-of-life dates, and switch to a newer model before then.
How it works
Building with Cortex Agents follows a five-step lifecycle:

Create an agent: Define the agent object in Snowsight, with SQL, or through the REST API, including its name, model, and instructions. See Create an agent.
Add tools: Configure the tools the agent can use and the resources each tool needs, such as semantic views, search services, and warehouses. See Add tools.
Test the agent: Prompt the agent in the Snowsight playground and refine its tools and instructions until it responds as expected. See Test the agent.
Integrate it into your application: Call the agent through the agent:run REST API, using threads to maintain conversation context. Users can also interact with agents directly in Snowflake CoWork and Cortex Code. See Cortex Agents Run API.
Monitor, evaluate, and iterate: Review threads, logs, and traces, collect end-user feedback as ratings and free-text comments, and run evaluations to refine the agent over its lifecycle. See Monitor Cortex Agent requests and Cortex Agent evaluations.

If you want to experiment before creating an agent object, you can call agent:run directly and pass the agent configuration with every request. See Create and manage agents.
When to use Cortex Agents
Cortex Agents is best for workloads that need:

Reasoning across structured and unstructured data: Questions whose answers combine SQL results over semantic views with retrieval from documents and other unstructured sources.
Multi-step task execution: Requests that the agent must break into subtasks, route to different tools, and reflect on intermediate results.
Minimal infrastructure: No orchestration loop, runtime, or sandbox to build or operate; Snowflake manages all of it.
Governance: Data access controlled by your existing Snowflake roles and privileges, and by the execution context of each configured tool.
Stateful conversations: Threads that persist context across turns without client-side state management.

Most tools run entirely inside Snowflake. Tools that reach external services, such as web search and MCP connectors, send requests over the public internet.

Tools
Cortex Agents supports the following tools:
ToolDescriptionCortex AnalystGenerates SQL queries over your structured data from natural language, using a semantic view.Cortex SearchRetrieves information from your unstructured data. Agents can dynamically adjust filters, retrieved columns, result counts, per-index queries, and time-decay settings based on the user’s query.Analytical search (Public Preview)Answers analytical questions, such as counts, aggregates, and trends, over large document collections by combining Cortex Search with AI functions and SQL. See Analytical search.Code executionRuns Python in a secure, isolated sandbox to process data and perform calculations.Data to ChartGenerates visualizations from data returned by other tools.Custom toolsStored procedures and user-defined functions (UDFs) that implement your own business logic or call backend systems.Agent skillsPackaged, modular bundles of instructions and scripts that give an agent repeatable, task-specific capabilities.MCP connectorsTools hosted on remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, such as those from Atlassian Jira, Salesforce, or your own applications.Agent toolsetsReferences to other agents whose tools are inherited at run time, enabling modular and composable agent architectures. See Agent toolsets.Web searchReal-time information from the public internet. Must be enabled at the account level. See Web search.ExpandShow lessSee more
For how to add and configure each tool, see Create and manage agents.
Access control and authentication
Calling an agent requires the SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER or SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_AGENT_USER database role, privileges on the agent object, and privileges on the objects used by the agent’s tools. If the user’s role is missing privileges on a tool, the request is rejected with a 4XX error. Cortex Agents determines session permissions from the querying user’s default role. Requests to the Cortex Agents API must include an authorization token.
For the full requirements, including role setup, privilege tables, and authentication methods, see Access control and authentication.
Limitations
Cortex Agents APIs are not supported from within a Streamlit in Snowflake (SiS) application using a warehouse runtime. To call Cortex Agents APIs from a SiS app, use a container runtime instead. For more information, see Runtime environments for Streamlit apps.

Cost considerations
Cortex Agents incurs charges for orchestration and for the tools the agent uses:

Orchestration is charged based on the tokens used.
Cortex Analyst is charged per token.
Cortex Search charges depend on the size of the index and the time it has persisted.
Custom tools incur warehouse costs, which depend on the size of the warehouse and how long it runs.
Analytical search adds warehouse compute for SQL execution, plus the AI functions it calls. These extra costs apply only when analytical search is enabled on the agent and the agent runs the analytical search loop.

This list isn’t exhaustive. Tools that run their own compute or call other services, including
web search, the
code execution tool,
MCP connectors, and
agent skills, can add cost beyond orchestration.
For the rates that apply to each feature, see the
Snowflake Service Consumption Table.
To limit what a single run consumes, set an orchestration budget on the agent. To monitor spend for an agent object and act when that spend crosses a threshold, use resource budgets. To enforce per-user credit limits for individual users, and optionally block users who reach their AI quota, use per-user quotas.

Legal notices
Where your configuration of Cortex Agents uses a model provided on the
Model and Service Flow-down Terms,
your use of that model is further subject to the terms for that model on that page.

For additional information, refer to Snowflake AI and ML.

-- ===========================================================================
-- 07_semantic / 01_semantic_view.sql
-- ===========================================================================
-- SV_RISK_COPILOT: the business model Cortex Analyst answers plain-English
-- questions from ("which branch had the most cash deposits?", "how many open
-- cases are high severity?").
--
-- What is deliberately NOT here:
--   * GROUND_TRUTH -- the labels. Nothing an analyst or a model can query may
--     reach the answer key (the label-leakage gate's rule).
--   * PAN, Aadhaar, phone, KYC free text -- masking policies need Enterprise;
--     until then the cheapest control is not to expose them at all.
--   * Counterparty/desk internals -- available in CURATED for detection, not
--     needed to answer business questions.
-- ===========================================================================
{% set ENR = fq.curated ~ "." ~ dt.transactions_enriched.name %}
{% set PARTY = fq.curated ~ "." ~ dt.dim_party.name %}

CREATE OR REPLACE SEMANTIC VIEW {{ fq.curated }}.{{ cortex.semantic_view }}
    TABLES (
        transactions AS {{ ENR }}
            PRIMARY KEY (txn_id)
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('payments', 'deposits', 'ledger')
            COMMENT = 'One row per transaction leg, in INR. A transfer has a debit (D) leg and a credit (C) leg.',
        customers AS {{ PARTY }}
            PRIMARY KEY (party_id)
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('parties', 'clients', 'account holders')
            COMMENT = 'Bank customers with their KYC profile.',
        cases AS {{ fq.evidence }}.CASE_RECORD
            PRIMARY KEY (case_id)
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('investigations', 'alerts')
            COMMENT = 'AML investigation cases, one per customer under investigation.',
        signals AS {{ fq.evidence }}.SIGNAL
            PRIMARY KEY (signal_id)
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('rule hits', 'detections')
            COMMENT = 'Detection rule firings that opened or support a case.',
        findings AS {{ fq.evidence }}.FINDING
            PRIMARY KEY (finding_id)
            COMMENT = 'Versioned investigation conclusions behind each STR.',
        strs AS {{ fq.evidence }}.ARTIFACT
            PRIMARY KEY (artifact_id)
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('suspicious transaction reports', 'filings', 'reports')
            COMMENT = 'Suspicious Transaction Report drafts and filings.'
    )
    RELATIONSHIPS (
        transaction_customer AS transactions (party_id) REFERENCES customers,
        case_customer AS cases (party_id) REFERENCES customers,
        signal_customer AS signals (party_id) REFERENCES customers,
        finding_case AS findings (case_id) REFERENCES cases,
        str_finding AS strs (finding_id) REFERENCES findings
    )
    FACTS (
        transactions.amount_inr AS amount_inr
            COMMENT = 'Leg amount in Indian rupees.',
        customers.declared_annual_income AS declared_annual_income
            COMMENT = 'Annual income the customer declared at KYC, in INR.',
        signals.metric_value AS metric_value
            COMMENT = 'The value the rule measured, e.g. distinct accounts used.'
    )
    DIMENSIONS (
        transactions.txn_id AS txn_id,
        transactions.txn_pair_id AS txn_pair_id
            COMMENT = 'Identifies one transaction; its debit and credit legs share it.',
        transactions.txn_date AS txn_date
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('date', 'transaction date'),
        transactions.txn_timestamp AS txn_timestamp,
        transactions.leg_side AS leg_side
            COMMENT = 'C = credit (money into the account), D = debit (money out).',
        transactions.channel AS channel
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('payment mode', 'payment channel')
            COMMENT = 'CASH, UPI, IMPS, NEFT, RTGS or CHEQUE.',
        transactions.txn_type AS txn_type
            COMMENT = 'DEPOSIT, PAYMENT or TRANSFER.',
        transactions.is_cash AS is_cash,
        transactions.account_id AS account_id,
        transactions.txn_branch_region AS branch_region
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('branch', 'region')
            COMMENT = 'Branch region of the account holder: MUMBAI, DELHI or PUNE.',
        customers.party_id AS party_id
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('customer id'),
        customers.customer_name AS full_name
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('name', 'customer'),
        customers.party_type AS party_type
            COMMENT = 'INDIVIDUAL or a business type.',
        customers.occupation AS occupation,
        customers.risk_rating AS risk_rating
            COMMENT = 'KYC risk rating: LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH.',
        customers.pep_flag AS pep_flag
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('politically exposed person'),
        customers.kyc_status AS kyc_status,
        customers.customer_branch_region AS branch_region,
        customers.customer_since AS customer_since,
        cases.case_id AS case_id,
        cases.case_status AS status
            COMMENT = 'OPEN, INVESTIGATING, DRAFTED, REVIEWED or CLOSED.',
        cases.case_type AS case_type,
        cases.case_branch_region AS branch_region,
        cases.opened_at AS opened_at,
        cases.sla_deadline AS sla_deadline
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('filing deadline'),
        signals.signal_id AS signal_id,
        signals.rule_id AS rule_id
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('rule', 'detection rule'),
        signals.severity AS severity,
        signals.window_bucket AS window_bucket,
        strs.artifact_id AS artifact_id,
        strs.str_status AS status
            COMMENT = 'DRAFT, REJECTED, REVIEWED, FILED, RETURNED or SUPERSEDED.',
        strs.str_created_at AS created_at
    )
    METRICS (
        transactions.total_amount_inr AS SUM(transactions.amount_inr)
            COMMENT = 'Sum of leg amounts in INR. Filter leg_side = C for money received.',
        transactions.transaction_count AS COUNT(DISTINCT transactions.txn_pair_id)
            COMMENT = 'Number of distinct transactions.',
        transactions.cash_deposit_amount_inr AS SUM(IFF(transactions.is_cash AND transactions.leg_side = 'C', transactions.amount_inr, 0))
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('cash deposited', 'cash deposits value')
            COMMENT = 'Total cash deposited into customer accounts, INR.',
        transactions.cash_deposit_count AS COUNT_IF(transactions.is_cash AND transactions.leg_side = 'C')
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('number of cash deposits'),
        customers.customer_count AS COUNT(customers.party_id),
        cases.case_count AS COUNT(cases.case_id)
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('number of cases'),
        signals.signal_count AS COUNT(signals.signal_id),
        strs.str_count AS COUNT(strs.artifact_id),
        strs.filed_str_count AS COUNT_IF(strs.str_status = 'FILED')
            WITH SYNONYMS = ('STRs filed', 'filed reports')
    )
    COMMENT = 'Risk & Compliance Copilot: transactions, customers, cases, signals and STRs. No ground-truth labels.';

"""Plain-English questions via Cortex Analyst over the semantic view.

Analyst turns a question into SQL against SV_RISK_COPILOT; the app runs that
SQL and shows it. The REST endpoint is called with the session's own token,
using the HTTP client bundled with the Snowflake connector, so the app needs
no extra package (the trial account has no external access to install one).
Every question is written to AUDIT.AGENT_ACTION_LOG with the SQL it produced.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import time
from typing import Any

from snowflake.connector.vendored import requests

from lib.db import CFG, S, session

ENDPOINT = "/api/v2/cortex/analyst/message"


def ask(question: str, history: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """One Analyst turn. Returns {text, sql, suggestions, request_id} or {error}."""
    conn = session().connection
    messages = [*history, {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": question}]}]
    started = time.time()
    try:
        r = requests.post(
            f"https://{conn.host}{ENDPOINT}",
            json={"messages": messages, "semantic_view": CFG["semantic_view"]},
            headers={
                "Authorization": f'Snowflake Token="{conn.rest.token}"',
                "Content-Type": "application/json",
                "Accept": "application/json",
            },
            timeout=120,
        )
    except Exception as exc:  # network path unavailable in this runtime
        return {"error": f"Cortex Analyst could not be reached: {exc}"}
    if not r.ok:
        return {"error": f"Cortex Analyst returned {r.status_code}: {r.text[:300]}"}
    body = r.json()
    out: dict[str, Any] = {
        "text": "",
        "sql": None,
        "suggestions": [],
        "request_id": body.get("request_id"),
        "message": body.get("message"),
        "latency_ms": int((time.time() - started) * 1000),
    }
    for part in (body.get("message") or {}).get("content", []):
        if part.get("type") == "text":
            out["text"] += part.get("text", "")
        elif part.get("type") == "sql":
            out["sql"] = part.get("statement")
        elif part.get("type") == "suggestions":
            out["suggestions"] = part.get("suggestions", [])
    return out


def log_turn(question: str, result: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Audit row for one question. Best effort: a logging failure must not hide the answer."""
    sql = result.get("sql")
    try:
        session().sql(
            f"""
            INSERT INTO {S['audit']}.AGENT_ACTION_LOG (
                log_id, session_id, turn_number, agent_mode, invoked_by, snowflake_user,
                user_role, question_text, tools_invoked, sql_text, sql_hash, model_version,
                prompt_version, latency_ms, outcome, error_text
            )
            SELECT 'LOG-' || UUID_STRING(), CURRENT_SESSION()::VARCHAR,
                   (SELECT COUNT(*) + 1 FROM {S['audit']}.AGENT_ACTION_LOG
                     WHERE session_id = CURRENT_SESSION()::VARCHAR),
                   'INVESTIGATOR', 'USER', CURRENT_USER(), CURRENT_ROLE(), ?,
                   ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('CORTEX_ANALYST'), ?, ?, 'CORTEX_ANALYST', ?, ?, ?, ?
            """,
            params=[
                question,
                sql,
                hashlib.sha256(sql.encode()).hexdigest() if sql else None,
                str(result.get("request_id") or "n/a"),
                result.get("latency_ms"),
                "ERROR" if result.get("error") else "SUCCESS",
                result.get("error"),
            ],
        ).collect()
    except Exception:  # noqa: S110 -- the audit row is best effort here
        pass

"""Ask: plain-English questions about transactions, customers, cases and STRs."""

import streamlit as st
from lib.analyst import ask, log_turn
from lib.db import query, reason

st.title("Ask the data")
st.caption(
    "Cortex Analyst writes the SQL from a governed semantic view (SV_RISK_COPILOT). The view "
    "excludes the answer key and identity numbers. You see the SQL behind every answer."
)

EXAMPLES = [
    "Which branch region received the most cash deposits by value?",
    "How many cases are there by status?",
    "Show the 5 customers with the highest total cash deposits",
    "How many cash deposits were made each day?",
]

if "ask_history" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["ask_history"] = []  # Analyst message format
    st.session_state["ask_turns"] = []  # what we render

cols = st.columns(len(EXAMPLES))
picked = None
for col, q in zip(cols, EXAMPLES, strict=True):
    if col.button(q, use_container_width=True):
        picked = q
typed = st.chat_input("Ask a question about the bank's data")
question = typed or picked

if question:
    with st.spinner("Cortex Analyst is writing the SQL..."):
        result = ask(question, st.session_state["ask_history"])
    log_turn(question, result)
    turn = {"q": question, **result}
    if result.get("sql"):
        try:
            turn["df"] = query(result["sql"])
        except Exception as exc:  # Analyst SQL that fails to run is shown, not hidden
            turn["run_error"] = reason(exc)
    st.session_state["ask_turns"].append(turn)
    if not result.get("error"):
        st.session_state["ask_history"] += [
            {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": question}]},
            result["message"],
        ]

for turn in reversed(st.session_state["ask_turns"]):
    with st.chat_message("user"):
        st.write(turn["q"])
    with st.chat_message("assistant"):
        if turn.get("error"):
            st.error(turn["error"])
            continue
        if turn.get("text"):
            st.write(turn["text"])
        df = turn.get("df")
        if df is not None:
            st.dataframe(df, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
            numeric = df.select_dtypes("number").columns.tolist()
            if len(df.columns) == 2 and len(numeric) == 1 and 1 < len(df) <= 50:
                label = next(c for c in df.columns if c not in numeric)
                st.bar_chart(df.set_index(label)[numeric[0]])
        if turn.get("run_error"):
            st.error(f"The generated SQL did not run: {turn['run_error']}")
        if turn.get("sql"):
            with st.expander("SQL written by Cortex Analyst"):
                st.code(turn["sql"], language="sql")
        for s in turn.get("suggestions") or []:
            st.caption(f"Try: {s}")
        st.caption(f"{turn.get('latency_ms', 0) / 1000:.1f}s · logged to AGENT_ACTION_LOG")

if st.session_state["ask_turns"] and st.button("Clear conversation"):
    st.session_state["ask_history"], st.session_state["ask_turns"] = [], []
    st.rerun()

"""SV_RISK_COPILOT (sql/07_semantic): what Cortex Analyst may and may not see."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from risk_copilot.config import load_settings
from risk_copilot.pipeline.deploy import Deployer, split_statements


def _view(repo_root: Path, profile: str = "dev") -> str:
    d = Deployer(load_settings(repo_root=repo_root, profile=profile))
    (path,) = d.stage_files("semantic")
    (statement,) = split_statements(d.render(path))
    return statement


@pytest.mark.parametrize("profile", ["dev", "demo"])
def test_the_view_is_named_from_config(repo_root: Path, profile: str) -> None:
    suffix = "_DEV" if profile == "dev" else ""
    db = f"RISK_COPILOT{suffix}"
    assert f"SEMANTIC VIEW {db}.CURATED.SV_RISK_COPILOT{suffix}" in _view(repo_root, profile)


def test_the_answer_key_is_unreachable(repo_root: Path) -> None:
    # The label-leakage rule: nothing an analyst or a model can query reaches GROUND_TRUTH.
    view = _view(repo_root)
    assert "GROUND_TRUTH" not in view
    assert not re.search(r"is_laundering|TXN_LABELS|EVAL_", view, re.IGNORECASE)


def test_identity_numbers_and_free_text_are_not_exposed(repo_root: Path) -> None:
    # No masking policies on Standard edition, so these simply are not in the view.
    view = _view(repo_root).lower()
    for column in ("pan_number", "aadhaar", "phone_number", "kyc_note", "source_ref"):
        assert column not in view, column
