## Demo runbook

Judges open the app in Snowsight (Projects > Streamlit > `RISK_COPILOT_APP_DEV`).
It runs in Streamlit in Snowflake on the container runtime, with the owner's
rights. Every button is one stored-procedure call, and every call writes a row
to `AUDIT.AGENT_ACTION_LOG`.

**Before the demo**

```bash
riskcopilot -p dev app reset-cases        # every case back to OPEN; shows what it deletes, then asks
riskcopilot -p dev app deploy             # only if app/ changed since the last deploy
```

`reset-cases` deletes the workflow's rows (EVIDENCE, EVIDENCE_QUERY_LOG, FINDING,
REVIEW, ARTIFACT, ATTESTATION) and reopens the cases, in one transaction. Signals
and case links are untouched. The audit log is kept, and the reset adds its own
row, so the trail shows both the earlier runs and the reset. This breaks the
evidence chain's append-only rule on purpose, so use it only on a demo database.

Then open the deployed app once and check that it loads. Also click through one
sign-off on a case you will not demo, then reset again. That sign-off has not yet
been exercised from inside Streamlit in Snowflake; Ask has, and works there.

**Click path** (times measured on the dev trial account, X-Small warehouse)

| # | Page | Action | Shows | Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Overview | -- | 5,032 transactions, 10 signals, 10 open cases, 0 STRs filed, recall / precision 10/10 | -- |

Plan: `.snowflake/cortex/plans/phase4-ship-demo-ui.plan.md`, approved 10-01. Trial
account ASHWINRAVI004 (ZC14131), dev profile only. Narratives are templated
(`TEMPLATE_V1`) because the trial blocks `AI_COMPLETE`.

## Status

| Step | Scope | State | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SiS prerequisites probe | **Done** | -- |
| 2 | Read-only app, deployed | **Done** | `f2172c6` |
| 3 | `GATHER_EVIDENCE`, `DRAFT_STR` | **Done** | `b52a86e` |
| 4 | `REVIEW_STR` | **Done** | `95f72c1` |
| 5 | `ATTEST_STR` | **Done** | `04b63be` |
| 6 | Workflow in the app | **Done** | `19b9d60` |
| 7 | Semantic view + Ask | **Done** | `fabb7c0` |
| -- | Container runtime fixes | **Done** | `88cc2f4`, `0c2a2fc` |
| 8 | `reset-cases`, rehearsal, runbook, docs | **Done**, except the streaming rehearsal (open item 1) | this commit |

## Decisions

| # | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D50 | The case tools are stored procedures, and the narrative is a governed template | The same procedures become `CREATE AGENT` tools once the account allows agents. Only the template step changes when `AI_COMPLETE` is available |
| D51 | The app is a thin client. Names reach it through `app/app_config.json`, rendered from `conf/`. Deploy is plain SQL: `PUT`, then `CREATE STREAMLIT` on the container runtime | The app cannot import `risk_copilot` in SiS. Plain SQL keeps deploy on the same key-pair session as every other command, with no Snowflake CLI |
| D52 | The app's packages come from `SNOWFLAKE.SNOWPARK.PYPI_SHARED_REPOSITORY` (`app.artifact_repository`) | M42. The trial has no external access, and this mirror needs none |
| D53 | `ATTEST_STR` runs `EXECUTE AS CALLER` and checks `IS_ROLE_IN_SESSION` (compliance role), REVIEWED + latest review APPROVE, and approved hash = stored hash = recomputed hash. It is the only setter of FILED | PML Rule 7. The gate is code, not an instruction to a model |
| D54 | The Reviewer is deterministic. It re-runs each logged query from its text and bind, then compares hashes and every figure | A critic that is a model can share the drafter's errors. A recompute cannot |
| D55 | `riskcopilot app reset-cases` deletes the six workflow tables and reopens the cases, in one transaction. It keeps SIGNAL, CASE_SIGNAL and the audit log, and logs itself as an OPERATOR row | The demo has to run more than once on the same ten cases. It breaks append-only on purpose, so it is a demo tool only |

## Measured facts

| # | Fact | Source |
|---|---|---|
| M42 | The container runtime will not start without `pyproject.toml` ("Installing dependencies failed because the pyproject.toml file does not exist"). With an empty dependency list it fails with "Failed to get the version of the Streamlit library ... >=1.48.0". It starts with `streamlit[snowflake]`, `pandas` and `altair` from the mirror | Deployed app, 10-02 |
| M43 | Inside SiS, `CURRENT_USER()` is the app's service user (`STPLATSTREAMLIT37820976`) and `CURRENT_ROLE()` is the owner, `RC_ADMIN_DEV`. An audit row written from SiS therefore names the app, not the viewer | Query history and AGENT_ACTION_LOG |
| M44 | Cortex Analyst works from inside SiS: the service user logged one successful CORTEX_ANALYST row (10-02 05:00 PDT). The app's page queries also succeed there | AGENT_ACTION_LOG, query history |
| M45 | `RC_ADMIN_DEV` holds `COMPLIANCE_OFFICER_DEV`, so `IS_ROLE_IN_SESSION` is true even with secondary roles off. In an owner's-rights app, the gate on the viewer is therefore the procedure's checks plus the typed, confirmed attestation, not the viewer's role | `SHOW GRANTS OF ROLE`, live |
| M46 | Rehearsal latencies (X-Small): gather 4.3 s (1.3-1.6 s re-run), draft 5.1 / 4.4 s, review 4.0 s, attest 1.9 s, Analyst 5.3 s | AGENT_ACTION_LOG.latency_ms |
| M47 | In the rehearsal, one Gather click logged 3 GATHER_EVIDENCE rows; the 2 extras came just before each Draft. Flipping the defect toggle alone did not reproduce it. Data is unaffected: the procedure is idempotent and inserted nothing | AGENT_ACTION_LOG |

## Steps 2-7

- **Step 2.** Overview (KPIs, case queue, signals, EVAL_RUN recall / precision), Case (KYC, the rule that fired, the deposits against the threshold) and Governance (clauses in force, rule registry, action log, eval runs). `riskcopilot app render | run | deploy`.

- **Step 5.** `ATTEST_STR` (D53). Refused live: a rejected draft, a bad decision, a blank attestor, an artifact edited after review, re-attesting, and redrafting after filing.
- **Step 6.** The case-page buttons, the Sign-off page (name + explicit confirmation, refusals shown verbatim, attestation register, a live "filed without attestation" count) and Overview's Live mode fragment. Driven headless with AppTest.
- **Step 7.** `SV_RISK_COPILOT` over transactions, customers, cases, signals, findings and STRs. It excludes GROUND_TRUTH, identity numbers and free text, since there is no masking on this edition. The Ask page calls Analyst over REST with the session token, runs the SQL, shows it, and logs it.
- **Fixes.** M42, then D52.

**What changed**

- Tests (`tests/unit/test_app.py`, +4):
  - deletes run children first, inside BEGIN/COMMIT, and every case field the procedures set is reset;

| 4 | A filed case | Gather, Draft, Review and the toggle are all disabled |

**Departures from the plan**

content.text:
Not as a command: `reset-cases` is a Python program on your laptop, and the Snowflake web UI can't run it. But all it does is SQL, so you can paste the equivalent into a Snowsight worksheet and get the same result.

**Steps**

1. Sign in to Snowsight as **ASHWINRAVI004**, the project account. The account this IDE is connected to doesn't have this database.
2. Go to **Projects > Worksheets** and click **+** to create a SQL worksheet.
3. Paste the preview script below and run it.
4. If the numbers look right, paste the reset script and run it with **Run All** (Ctrl+Shift+Enter, or the arrow next to Run). It has to run as a whole, so the `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` wraps everything.

**Preview (changes nothing)**

```sql
USE ROLE RC_ADMIN_DEV;
USE WAREHOUSE RC_DEV_WH_DEV;

SELECT 'ATTESTATION' AS tbl, COUNT(*) AS n_rows FROM RISK_COPILOT_DEV.EVIDENCE_CHAIN.ATTESTATION
UNION ALL SELECT 'REVIEW', COUNT(*) FROM RISK_COPILOT_DEV.EVIDENCE_CHAIN.REVIEW
UNION ALL SELECT 'ARTIFACT', COUNT(*) FROM RISK_COPILOT_DEV.EVIDENCE_CHAIN.ARTIFACT
UNION ALL SELECT 'FINDING', COUNT(*) FROM RISK_COPILOT_DEV.EVIDENCE_CHAIN.FINDING
UNION ALL SELECT 'EVIDENCE_QUERY_LOG', COUNT(*) FROM RISK_COPILOT_DEV.EVIDENCE_CHAIN.EVIDENCE_QUERY_LOG
UNION ALL SELECT 'EVIDENCE', COUNT(*) FROM RISK_COPILOT_DEV.EVIDENCE_CHAIN.EVIDENCE
UNION ALL SELECT 'CASES TO REOPEN', COUNT(*) FROM RISK_COPILOT_DEV.EVIDENCE_CHAIN.CASE_RECORD
  WHERE NOT (status = 'OPEN' AND suspicion_established_at IS NULL AND sla_deadline IS NULL
             AND closed_at IS NULL AND closure_reason IS NULL);
```

**Reset (run all at once)**

```sql
USE ROLE RC_ADMIN_DEV;
USE WAREHOUSE RC_DEV_WH_DEV;
USE SCHEMA RISK_COPILOT_DEV.EVIDENCE_CHAIN;

BEGIN;

-- 1. Record the reset in the audit log first, while the counts still exist.
INSERT INTO RISK_COPILOT_DEV.AUDIT.AGENT_ACTION_LOG (
    log_id, session_id, turn_number, agent_mode, invoked_by, snowflake_user, user_role,
    tools_invoked, tool_arguments, case_ids_touched, model_version, prompt_version,
    rows_touched, outcome
)
SELECT 'LOG-' || UUID_STRING(), CURRENT_SESSION()::VARCHAR,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) + 1 FROM RISK_COPILOT_DEV.AUDIT.AGENT_ACTION_LOG
         WHERE session_id = CURRENT_SESSION()::VARCHAR),
       'OPERATOR', 'USER', CURRENT_USER(), CURRENT_ROLE(),
       ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('RESET_CASES'),
       OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('via', 'SNOWSIGHT', 'deleted', OBJECT_CONSTRUCT(
           'ATTESTATION', c.att, 'REVIEW', c.rev, 'ARTIFACT', c.art, 'FINDING', c.fnd,
           'EVIDENCE_QUERY_LOG', c.qlg, 'EVIDENCE', c.evd)),
       c.case_ids, 'n/a', 'n/a',
       c.att + c.rev + c.art + c.fnd + c.qlg + c.evd + ARRAY_SIZE(c.case_ids), 'SUCCESS'
FROM (
    SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ATTESTATION) AS att,
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM REVIEW) AS rev,
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ARTIFACT) AS art,
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM FINDING) AS fnd,
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM EVIDENCE_QUERY_LOG) AS qlg,
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM EVIDENCE) AS evd,
           (SELECT COALESCE(ARRAY_AGG(case_id) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY case_id), ARRAY_CONSTRUCT())
              FROM CASE_RECORD
             WHERE NOT (status = 'OPEN' AND suspicion_established_at IS NULL AND sla_deadline IS NULL
                        AND closed_at IS NULL AND closure_reason IS NULL)) AS case_ids
) c;

-- 2. Delete the workflow rows, children first.
DELETE FROM ATTESTATION;
DELETE FROM REVIEW;
DELETE FROM ARTIFACT;
DELETE FROM FINDING;
DELETE FROM EVIDENCE_QUERY_LOG;
DELETE FROM EVIDENCE;

-- 3. Put every case back the way the router opened it.
UPDATE CASE_RECORD
SET status = 'OPEN', suspicion_established_at = NULL, sla_deadline = NULL,
    closed_at = NULL, closure_reason = NULL,
    updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()::TIMESTAMP_NTZ
WHERE NOT (status = 'OPEN' AND suspicion_established_at IS NULL AND sla_deadline IS NULL
           AND closed_at IS NULL AND closure_reason IS NULL);

COMMIT;
```

Afterwards, run the preview again: every row should show 0. The app picks up the change within about 10 seconds of a page refresh.

**How it differs from the CLI command**
- There's no confirmation prompt. The preview script stands in for it, so run that first.
- If a statement fails partway, run `ROLLBACK;` before trying again, and nothing will have changed. The CLI does that rollback for you automatically.
- The audit row records `"via": "SNOWSIGHT"`, so in the log you can tell which way a reset was run.

1|"""Plain-English questions via Cortex Analyst over the semantic view.
     2|
     3|Analyst turns a question into SQL against SV_RISK_COPILOT; the app runs that
     4|SQL and shows it. The REST endpoint is called with the session's own token,
     5|using the HTTP client bundled with the Snowflake connector, so the app needs
     6|no extra package (the trial account has no external access to install one).
     7|Every question is written to AUDIT.AGENT_ACTION_LOG with the SQL it produced.
     8|"""
     9|
    10|from __future__ import annotations
    11|
    12|import contextlib
    13|import hashlib
    14|import time
    15|from typing import Any
    16|
    17|from snowflake.connector.vendored import requests
    18|
    19|from lib.db import CFG, S, session
    20|
    21|ENDPOINT = "/api/v2/cortex/analyst/message"
    22|
    23|
    24|def ask(question: str, history: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    25|    """One Analyst turn. Returns {text, sql, suggestions, request_id} or {error}."""
    26|    conn = session().connection
    27|    messages = [*history, {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": question}]}]
    28|    started = time.time()
    29|    try:
    30|        r = requests.post(
    31|            f"https://{conn.host}{ENDPOINT}",
    32|            json={"messages": messages, "semantic_view": CFG["semantic_view"]},
    33|            headers={
    34|                "Authorization": f'Snowflake Token="{conn.rest.token}"',
    35|                "Content-Type": "application/json",
    36|                "Accept": "application/json",
    37|            },
    38|            timeout=120,
    39|        )
    40|    except Exception as exc:  # network path unavailable in this runtime
    41|        return {"error": f"Cortex Analyst could not be reached: {exc}"}
    42|    if not r.ok:
    43|        return {"error": f"Cortex Analyst returned {r.status_code}: {r.text[:300]}"}
    44|    body = r.json()
    45|    out: dict[str, Any] = {
    46|        "text": "",
    47|        "sql": None,
    48|        "suggestions": [],
    49|        "request_id": body.get("request_id"),
    50|        "message": body.get("message"),
    51|        "latency_ms": int((time.time() - started) * 1000),
    52|    }
    53|    for part in (body.get("message") or {}).get("content", []):
    54|        if part.get("type") == "text":
    55|            out["text"] += part.get("text", "")
    56|        elif part.get("type") == "sql":
    57|            out["sql"] = part.get("statement")
    58|        elif part.get("type") == "suggestions":
    59|            out["suggestions"] = part.get("suggestions", [])
    60|    return out
    61|
    62|
    63|def log_turn(question: str, result: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    64|    """Audit row for one question. Best effort: a logging failure must not hide the answer."""
    65|    sql = result.get("sql")
    66|    with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
    67|        session().sql(
    68|            f"""
    69|            INSERT INTO {S["audit"]}.AGENT_ACTION_LOG (
    70|                log_id, session_id, turn_number, agent_mode, invoked_by, snowflake_user,
    71|                user_role, question_text, tools_invoked, sql_text, sql_hash, model_version,
    72|                prompt_version, latency_ms, outcome, error_text
    73|            )
    74|            SELECT 'LOG-' || UUID_STRING(), CURRENT_SESSION()::VARCHAR,
    75|                   (SELECT COUNT(*) + 1 FROM {S["audit"]}.AGENT_ACTION_LOG
    76|                     WHERE session_id = CURRENT_SESSION()::VARCHAR),
    77|                   'INVESTIGATOR', 'USER', CURRENT_USER(), CURRENT_ROLE(), ?,
    78|                   ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('CORTEX_ANALYST'), ?, ?, 'CORTEX_ANALYST', ?, ?, ?, ?
    79|            """,
    80|            params=[
    81|                question,
    82|                sql,
    83|                hashlib.sha256(sql.encode()).hexdigest() if sql else None,
    84|                str(result.get("request_id") or "n/a"),
    85|                result.get("latency_ms"),
    86|                "ERROR" if result.get("error") else "SUCCESS",
    87|                result.get("error"),
    88|            ],
    89|        ).collect()
    90|

"""Demo sign-in: two personas, so maker-checker is visible in the UI.

This is a demonstration of the security model, not the security model itself.
The credentials are shown on the sign-in page on purpose, so a judge is never
blocked. What a real deployment does instead, and what holds regardless of
this page, is listed in SECURITY_NOTES.

The control that matters is in the database: ATTEST_STR refuses unless the
review approved this exact content hash, whoever is signed in here.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import hmac
from typing import Any

import streamlit as st

#: username -> persona. Passwords are compared as SHA-256 digests, in constant time.
PERSONAS: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {
    "analyst": {
        "name": "Priya Nair",
        "title": "AML Analyst",
        "duty": "Investigates, drafts and reviews STRs. Cannot sign.",
        "icon": ":material/manage_search:",
        "can_investigate": True,
        "can_attest": False,
        "sha256": "7b3d4b4d9b0b3fbd1a63a6bd7f1b8c19c9fd2d78d1c1c25f4a2c11d4d8d1d3a1",
    },
    "officer": {
        "name": "Rajesh Menon",
        "title": "Principal Officer",
        "duty": "Signs or returns approved STRs. Does not draft them.",
        "icon": ":material/verified:",
        "can_investigate": False,
        "can_attest": True,
        "sha256": "",
    },
}

#: Shown on the sign-in page. Demo only -- see SECURITY_NOTES.
DEMO_PASSWORDS = {"analyst": "Analyst@2026", "officer": "Officer@2026"}

SECURITY_NOTES = [
    "**Maker-checker.** The analyst who drafts an STR cannot sign it; only the Principal "
    "Officer can (PML Rules, Rule 7). The app hides the other role's controls.",
    "**Enforced in the database too.** `ATTEST_STR` refuses unless the Reviewer approved "
    "this exact version and its SHA-256 still matches. Filing is impossible from any screen "
    "without a matching, hash-bound attestation.",
    "**Least privilege.** The hosted app connects as a dedicated service user that can read "
    "the demo data and run the case tools, and nothing else. It never sees the answer key.",
    "**Every action is logged** to `AUDIT.AGENT_ACTION_LOG`, including refusals and resets.",
    "**In production** this page is replaced by the bank's SSO (Snowflake SAML or OAuth), and "
    "each officer acts under their own Snowflake role (restricted caller's rights).",
]

_SESSION_KEY = "auth_user"


def _digest(password: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(password.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


# The digests are derived once from the demo passwords, so the two can never drift.
for _user, _password in DEMO_PASSWORDS.items():
    PERSONAS[_user]["sha256"] = _digest(_password)


def sign_in(username: str, password: str) -> bool:
    user = PERSONAS.get(username.strip().lower())
    if not user or not hmac.compare_digest(_digest(password), user["sha256"]):
        return False
    st.session_state[_SESSION_KEY] = username.strip().lower()
    return True


def sign_out(prefill: str | None = None) -> None:
    """Sign out; optionally pre-fill the sign-in form for another persona."""
    st.session_state.pop(_SESSION_KEY, None)
    if prefill:
        fill(prefill)


def fill(username: str) -> None:
    """Put a persona's demo credentials into the sign-in form (an on_click callback)."""
    st.session_state["login_user"] = username
    st.session_state["login_password"] = DEMO_PASSWORDS[username]


def current() -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    key = st.session_state.get(_SESSION_KEY)
    return {"username": key, **PERSONAS[key]} if key in PERSONAS else None


def can(permission: str) -> bool:
    user = current()
    return bool(user and user.get(permission))

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Public access -- the service user Streamlit Community Cloud connects as
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

#: Where the key pair and the secrets file go: outside the repository, always.
DEFAULT_KEY_DIR = Path.home() / ".snowflake" / "keys"
_B64 = frozenset("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/=")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PublicAccess:
    user: str
    role: str
    warehouse: str
    key_file: Path
    secrets_file: Path
    key_created: bool
    checks: dict[str, Any]


def _key_pair(key_file: Path) -> tuple[bytes, str, bool]:
    """(PKCS8 PEM private key, base64 DER public key, created). Reuses an existing key."""
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa

    created = not key_file.is_file()
    if created:
        key = rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)
        pem = key.private_bytes(
            serialization.Encoding.PEM,
            serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,
            serialization.NoEncryption(),
        )
        key_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        key_file.write_bytes(pem)
    pem = key_file.read_bytes()
    private = serialization.load_pem_private_key(pem, password=None)
    der = private.public_key().public_bytes(
        serialization.Encoding.DER, serialization.PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo
    )
    import base64

    return pem, base64.b64encode(der).decode("ascii"), created


def secrets_toml(*, account: str, user: str, role: str, warehouse: str, database: str,
                 pem: bytes) -> str:
    """The [snowflake] section lib/db.py reads on Streamlit Community Cloud."""
    for name, value in (("account", account), ("user", user), ("role", role),
                        ("warehouse", warehouse), ("database", database)):
        if not value or '"' in value or "\n" in value:
            raise AppError(f"Refusing to write secrets: bad {name} {value!r}")
    return (
        "# Streamlit Community Cloud > your app > Settings > Secrets: paste this file.\n"
        "# It holds a private key. Never commit it; rotate with `riskcopilot app public-access`.\n"
        "[snowflake]\n"
        f'account = "{account}"\n'
        f'user = "{user}"\n'
        f'role = "{role}"\n'
        f'warehouse = "{warehouse}"\n'
        f'database = "{database}"\n'
        f'private_key_pem = """\n{pem.decode("ascii").strip()}\n"""\n'
    )


def provision_public_access(
    settings: Settings, session: Any, *, key_dir: Path = DEFAULT_KEY_DIR,
    account: str, rotate: bool = False,
) -> PublicAccess:
    """Create (or update) the hosted app's service user and write its secrets file.

    The user is TYPE = SERVICE with only a public key: it cannot sign in with a
    password or interactively. Its role is granted by the app_access stage.
    """
    if not settings.app.public_user or not settings.roles.public_app:
        raise AppError("Set conf/base.yml app.public_user and roles.public_app first.")
    user = settings.obj(settings.app.public_user)
    role = settings.obj(settings.roles.public_app)
    warehouse = settings.obj(settings.warehouse(settings.app.warehouse).name)
    key_file = key_dir / f"{user.lower()}.p8"
    if rotate and key_file.is_file():
        key_file.unlink()
    pem, public_b64, created = _key_pair(key_file)
    if not set(public_b64) <= _B64:  # it is interpolated into ALTER USER below
        raise AppError("Public key is not base64; refusing to continue.")

    execute(session, "USE ROLE ACCOUNTADMIN")
    try:
        execute(
            session,
            f"CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS {user} TYPE = SERVICE "
            "COMMENT = 'Streamlit Community Cloud demo app. Key pair only.'",
        )
        execute(
            session,
            f"ALTER USER {user} SET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY = '{public_b64}' "
            f"DEFAULT_ROLE = {role} DEFAULT_WAREHOUSE = {warehouse}",
        )
        execute(session, f"GRANT ROLE {role} TO USER {user}")
    finally:
        execute(session, f"USE ROLE {settings.obj(settings.roles.admin)}")

    secrets_file = key_dir / f"{user.lower()}.streamlit-secrets.toml"
    secrets_file.write_text(
        secrets_toml(account=account, user=user, role=role, warehouse=warehouse,
                     database=settings.db(), pem=pem),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    return PublicAccess(user, role, warehouse, key_file, secrets_file, created, checks={})


def check_public_access(settings: Settings, secrets_file: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Sign in exactly as the hosted app will, and run what its pages run."""
    import tomllib

    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
    from snowflake.snowpark import Session

    cfg = dict(tomllib.loads(secrets_file.read_text("utf-8"))["snowflake"])
    key = serialization.load_pem_private_key(cfg.pop("private_key_pem").encode(), password=None)
    cfg["private_key"] = key.private_bytes(
        serialization.Encoding.DER,
        serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,
        serialization.NoEncryption(),
    )
    s = Session.builder.configs(cfg).create()
    try:
        ev = settings.fq("evidence")
        who = s.sql("SELECT CURRENT_USER(), CURRENT_ROLE(), CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()").collect()[0]
        cases = s.sql(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {ev}.CASE_RECORD").collect()[0][0]
        scores = s.sql(
            f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {settings.fq('curated', settings.views['eval_scores'])}"
        ).collect()[0][0]
        proc = settings.fq("evidence", settings.case_tools["reset_cases"])
        dry = s.sql(f"CALL {proc}('CHECK', TRUE)").collect()[0][0]
        try:
            s.sql(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {settings.fq('ground_truth')}.TXN_LABELS").collect()
            labels = "READABLE"
        except Exception:
            labels = "refused"
        return {
            "user": who[0], "role": who[1], "warehouse": who[2], "cases": int(cases),
            "eval_runs": int(scores), "reset_dry_run": "ok" if dry else "empty",
            "ground_truth_labels": labels,
        }
    finally:
        s.close()

def app_public_access(
    rotate: Annotated[
        bool, typer.Option("--rotate", help="Replace the key pair (the old key stops working).")
    ] = False,
) -> None:
    """Create the hosted app's service user and write its Streamlit secrets file.

    Run `deploy --stage app_access` first (the role and its grants). The key pair
    and the secrets file are written under ~/.snowflake/keys, never the repo.
    Then it signs in as that user and checks what the hosted app will do.
    """
    from risk_copilot.pipeline.app import (
        AppError,
        check_public_access,
        provision_public_access,
    )
    from risk_copilot.session import SessionError, build_connect_params, open_session

    settings = _settings()
    try:
        account = str(build_connect_params(settings)["account"])
        with open_session(settings, unattended=True) as session:
            result = provision_public_access(settings, session, account=account, rotate=rotate)
        checks = check_public_access(settings, result.secrets_file)
    except (AppError, SessionError, KeyError) as exc:
        console.print(f"[red]Public access failed[/red]\n{exc}")
        raise typer.Exit(code=1) from exc
    console.print(
        f"[green]Service user[/green] {result.user} (role {result.role}, warehouse "
        f"{result.warehouse}); key {'created' if result.key_created else 'reused'}."

"""Data access for the app: one session, parameterised queries, config-driven names.

Runs in three places with one code path; only the session differs:

* Streamlit Community Cloud -- a ``[snowflake]`` section in the app's secrets
  (written by ``riskcopilot app public-access``): a key-pair service user with a
  least-privilege role. No visitor needs a Snowflake account.
* Locally (``riskcopilot app run``) -- the package is installed, so the session
  comes from the same key-pair connection every other command uses.
* Streamlit in Snowflake -- ``st.connection("snowflake")`` gives the app owner's
  session. The ``risk_copilot`` package is not uploaded, so its import fails.

Identifiers come from ``app_config.json`` (rendered from conf/, validated
there); values are always bound, never interpolated.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

CFG: dict[str, Any] = json.loads(
    (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "app_config.json").read_text("utf-8")
)
S: dict[str, str] = CFG["schema"]
DT: dict[str, str] = CFG["dt"]
VIEW: dict[str, str] = CFG["view"]
PROC: dict[str, str] = CFG["procedure"]
HERO: dict[str, Any] | None = CFG.get("hero")


def _secrets() -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """The hosted app's [snowflake] secrets, or None (no secrets file is normal)."""
    try:
        return dict(st.secrets["snowflake"]) if "snowflake" in st.secrets else None
    except Exception:  # no secrets.toml at all: local or Streamlit in Snowflake
        return None


def _secrets_session(cfg: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
    from snowflake.snowpark import Session

    key = serialization.load_pem_private_key(cfg.pop("private_key_pem").encode(), password=None)
    cfg["private_key"] = key.private_bytes(
        serialization.Encoding.DER,
        serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,
        serialization.NoEncryption(),
    )
    cfg["authenticator"] = "SNOWFLAKE_JWT"
    cfg.setdefault("application", "risk_copilot_app")
    return Session.builder.configs(cfg).create()


@st.cache_resource(show_spinner=False)
def session() -> Any:
    if (cfg := _secrets()) is not None:  # Streamlit Community Cloud
        return _secrets_session(cfg)
    try:
        from risk_copilot.config import load_settings
        from risk_copilot.session import create_session
    except ImportError:  # Streamlit in Snowflake
        return st.connection("snowflake").session()
    return create_session(load_settings(), unattended=True)

"""The sign-in screen. The demo credentials are on it on purpose: see lib/auth.py.

Rendered in place of whichever page was requested, so a deep link (or the
officer switching in from sign-off) lands back on that page after signing in.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import streamlit as st

from lib import auth
from lib.db import CFG


def render() -> None:
    st.title(CFG["title"])
    st.markdown(
        "From a suspicious pattern to a regulator-ready **Suspicious Transaction Report**, "
        "with every figure proven in SQL and a human signature on every filing."
    )

    left, right = st.columns([5, 6], gap="large")
    with left, st.container(border=True):
        st.subheader("Sign in")
        with st.form("sign_in", border=False):
            username = st.text_input("Username", key="login_user")
            password = st.text_input("Password", type="password", key="login_password")
            submitted = st.form_submit_button("Sign in", type="primary", use_container_width=True)
        if submitted:
            if auth.sign_in(username, password):
                st.rerun()
            st.error("Those credentials do not match a demo user. Use one of the accounts shown.")

    with right:
        st.subheader("Demo accounts")
        st.caption("Copy the credentials, or click **Use** to fill the form. Two roles, two duties.")
        for key, persona in auth.PERSONAS.items():
            with st.container(border=True):
                head, use = st.columns([4, 1], vertical_alignment="center")
                head.markdown(f"{persona['icon']} **{persona['title']}** · {persona['name']}")
                use.button(
                    "Use",
                    key=f"use_{key}",
                    on_click=auth.fill,
                    args=(key,),
                    use_container_width=True,
                )
                st.caption(persona["duty"])
                u, p = st.columns(2)
                with u:
                    st.code(key, language=None)
                with p:
                    st.code(auth.DEMO_PASSWORDS[key], language=None)

    with st.expander("Security model: what this page shows, and what a bank would use"):
        for note in auth.SECURITY_NOTES:
            st.markdown(f"- {note}")

"""Hosting the app on Streamlit Community Cloud, and the demo sign-in.

The hosted app runs from the repository as committed, so what it reads there
(app_config.json, requirements.txt, the theme) must not drift from conf/ and
from what Streamlit in Snowflake installs. Its service role must be able to
run every case tool and nothing on GROUND_TRUTH.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest

from risk_copilot.config import load_settings
from risk_copilot.pipeline.app import AppError, app_config, secrets_toml
from risk_copilot.pipeline.deploy import Deployer, split_statements


def test_the_committed_app_config_matches_conf(repo_root: Path) -> None:
    # Community Cloud cannot run `riskcopilot app render`: it reads the file in git.
    committed = json.loads((repo_root / "app" / "app_config.json").read_text("utf-8"))
    assert committed == app_config(load_settings(repo_root=repo_root, profile="dev")), (
        "app/app_config.json is stale: run `riskcopilot -p dev app render` and commit it"
    )


def test_requirements_match_the_streamlit_in_snowflake_dependencies(repo_root: Path) -> None:
    project = tomllib.loads((repo_root / "app" / "pyproject.toml").read_text("utf-8"))

def _signatures(sql: str) -> dict[str, tuple[str, ...]]:
    """Procedure name -> argument types, from CREATE PROCEDURE statements."""
    out: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
    for m in re.finditer(r"CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE\s+([\w.]+)\s*\((.*?)\)\s*RETURNS", sql, re.S):
        args = [a.split()[1].upper() for a in m.group(2).split(",") if a.strip()]
        out[m.group(1).upper()] = tuple(args)
    return out


def test_the_public_role_can_run_every_case_tool(repo_root: Path) -> None:
    deployer = Deployer(load_settings(repo_root=repo_root, profile="dev"))
    procs: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
    for path in deployer.stage_files("procedures"):
        procs |= _signatures(deployer.render(path))
    grants = {}
    for path in deployer.stage_files("app_access"):
        for m in re.finditer(r"GRANT USAGE ON PROCEDURE ([\w.]+)\(([^)]*)\)", deployer.render(path)):
            grants[m.group(1).upper()] = tuple(t.strip().upper() for t in m.group(2).split(","))
    assert grants, "the app_access stage grants no procedure"
    # Each grant names a real signature; a mismatch fails only at deploy time otherwise.
    for name, types in grants.items():
        assert procs.get(name) == types, f"{name}{types} does not match {procs.get(name)}"
    tools = {deployer.settings.fq("evidence", t).upper() for t in deployer.settings.case_tools.values()}
    assert tools & set(procs) <= set(grants), "a case tool the app calls is not granted"


def test_the_public_role_gets_nothing_on_ground_truth(repo_root: Path) -> None:
    deployer = Deployer(load_settings(repo_root=repo_root, profile="dev"))
    gt = deployer.settings.fq("ground_truth").upper()
    for path in deployer.stage_files("app_access"):
        for statement in split_statements(deployer.render(path)):
            if statement.lstrip().upper().startswith("GRANT"):
                assert gt not in statement.upper(), statement


def test_secrets_refuse_values_that_would_break_the_file() -> None:
    good = dict(account="A", user="U", role="R", warehouse="W", database="D")
    text = secrets_toml(**good, pem=b"-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nabc\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----")
    parsed = tomllib.loads(text)["snowflake"]
    assert parsed["user"] == "U" and parsed["private_key_pem"].strip().startswith("-----BEGIN")
    with pytest.raises(AppError, match="bad role"):
        secrets_toml(**{**good, "role": 'R"\nx = "y'}, pem=b"k")

151|## Demo runbook
   152|
   153|Judges open the app in Snowsight (Projects > Streamlit > `RISK_COPILOT_APP_DEV`).
   154|It runs in Streamlit in Snowflake on the container runtime, with the owner's
   155|rights. Every button is one stored-procedure call, and every call writes a row
   156|to `AUDIT.AGENT_ACTION_LOG`.
   157|
   158|**Before the demo**, reset every case. All three ways call the same procedure,
   159|`EVIDENCE_CHAIN.RESET_CASES_DEV`, and each shows what it will delete first:
   160|
   161|- **In the app:** Governance & audit > *Demo controls: reset every case*, then type `RESET`.
   162|- **In a Snowsight worksheet:** `CALL RISK_COPILOT_DEV.EVIDENCE_CHAIN.RESET_CASES_DEV('SQL', TRUE);`
   163|  previews the reset, and `CALL ...RESET_CASES_DEV('SQL', FALSE);` runs it.
   164|- **From the CLI:** `riskcopilot -p dev app reset-cases`, which asks before it runs.
   165|
   166|Run `riskcopilot -p dev app deploy` only if `app/` changed since the last deploy.
   167|
   168|The reset deletes the workflow's rows (EVIDENCE, EVIDENCE_QUERY_LOG, FINDING,
   169|REVIEW, ARTIFACT, ATTESTATION) and reopens the cases, in one transaction. Signals
   170|and case links are untouched. The audit log is kept, and the reset adds its own
   171|row, recording where it was run from (`via`). This breaks the evidence chain's
   172|append-only rule on purpose, so use it only on a demo database.
   173|
   174|Then open the deployed app once and check that it loads. Also click through one
   175|sign-off on a case you will not demo, then reset again. That sign-off has not yet
   176|been exercised from inside Streamlit in Snowflake; Ask has, and works there.

   184|| 3 | Case | **1 · Gather evidence** | Status INVESTIGATING; 18 evidence pointers, 4 logged queries with hashes | ~4 s |
   185|| 4 | Case | Turn on **Plant a defect**, then **2 · Draft STR** | Draft v1 claims ₹1,03,42,961 and cites `CTR_CASH_THRESHOLD_2026` | ~5 s |
   186|| 5 | Case | **3 · Run Reviewer** | **REJECT**, with 2 defects: the stated total vs the ₹94,02,691 its query returns, and a clause that does not exist. 4 queries re-run, no model | ~4 s |
   187|| 6 | Case | Turn the defect off, then **2 · Draft STR**, then **3 · Run Reviewer** | v2 states ₹94,02,691 and gets **APPROVE**: all 4 checks pass; v1 stays in the version history | ~9 s |
   188|| 7 | Case | **Go to sign-off** | The approved STR, its hash, the Reviewer's checklist | -- |
   189|| 8 | Sign-off | Name, Attest, **Sign** without ticking the box | Refused: "Tick the confirmation to sign." | -- |
   190|| 9 | Sign-off | Tick, **Sign** | ATTESTED: the STR is FILED, the attestation records its hash; "filed without attestation" stays 0 | ~2 s |
   191|| 10 | Ask the data | "How many cases are there by status?" | Cortex Analyst's SQL and a chart: 1 CLOSED, 9 OPEN | ~5 s |

## Demo runbook

The same app runs in two hosted places:

- **Streamlit Community Cloud**, a public URL that needs no Snowflake account. It
  connects as the key-pair service user `RC_PUBLIC_APP_USER_DEV`, whose role can read
  the demo and run the case tools and nothing else. To host it:
  1. Run `riskcopilot -p dev deploy --stage app_access` and
     `riskcopilot -p dev app public-access` (it signs in as the user and checks it).
  2. Push the branch.
  3. At share.streamlit.io, create an app from the repository. Set the main file to
     `app/streamlit_app.py` and Python to 3.11.
  4. Paste `~/.snowflake/keys/rc_public_app_user_dev.streamlit-secrets.toml` into
     Settings > Secrets. Never commit that file.
- **Streamlit in Snowflake**, in Snowsight under Projects > Streamlit >
  `RISK_COPILOT_APP_DEV`. It runs on the container runtime with the owner's rights.

Both open on a sign-in page that shows the two demo accounts. The **AML Analyst**
(`analyst` / `Analyst@2026`) investigates, drafts and reviews. The **Principal
Officer** (`officer` / `Officer@2026`) signs. Each persona sees only their own
duty's controls (maker-checker).

Every button is one stored-procedure call, and every call writes a row to
`AUDIT.AGENT_ACTION_LOG`.

        )

        present = [o for o in outcomes if o in set(tl["outcome"])]
        others = sorted(set(tl["outcome"]) - set(outcomes))
        chart = (
            alt.Chart(tl)
            .mark_point(filled=True, size=140, opacity=0.85)
            .encode(
                x=alt.X("logged_at:T", title=None),
                y=alt.Y("tool:N", title=None, sort="-x"),
                color=alt.Color(
                    "outcome:N",
                    title="Outcome",
                    scale=alt.Scale(
                        domain=present + others,
                        range=[outcomes[o] for o in present] + [ui.SLATE] * len(others),
                    ),
                    legend=alt.Legend(orient="bottom"),
                ),
                shape=alt.Shape("agent_mode:N", title="Actor", legend=alt.Legend(orient="bottom")),

                    alt.Tooltip("logged_at:T", format="%d %b %H:%M:%S"),

                    "outcome:N",
                    "refusal_reason:N",
                    "latency_ms:Q",
                ],
            )
            .properties(height={"step": 34})

**2. Public hosting.** The hosted app connects as a dedicated service user, `RC_PUBLIC_APP_USER_DEV`, so visitors need no Snowflake account.

- Its role can read the demo data and run the five case tools, and nothing else.

1|"""Data access for the app: one session, parameterised queries, config-driven names.
     2|
     3|Runs in three places with one code path; only the session differs:
     4|
     5|* Streamlit Community Cloud -- a ``[snowflake]`` section in the app's secrets
     6|  (written by ``riskcopilot app public-access``): a key-pair service user with a
     7|  least-privilege role. No visitor needs a Snowflake account.
     8|* Locally (``riskcopilot app run``) -- the package is installed, so the session
     9|  comes from the same key-pair connection every other command uses.
    10|* Streamlit in Snowflake -- ``st.connection("snowflake")`` gives the app owner's
    11|  session. The ``risk_copilot`` package is not uploaded, so its import fails.
    12|
    13|Identifiers come from ``app_config.json`` (rendered from conf/, validated
    14|there); values are always bound, never interpolated.
    15|"""

    18|
    19|import json
    20|from pathlib import Path
    21|from typing import Any
    22|
    23|import pandas as pd
    24|import streamlit as st
    25|
    26|CFG: dict[str, Any] = json.loads(
    27|    (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "app_config.json").read_text("utf-8")
    28|)
    29|S: dict[str, str] = CFG["schema"]
    30|DT: dict[str, str] = CFG["dt"]
    31|VIEW: dict[str, str] = CFG["view"]
    32|PROC: dict[str, str] = CFG["procedure"]
    33|HERO: dict[str, Any] | None = CFG.get("hero")
    34|
    35|
    36|def _secrets() -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    37|    """The hosted app's [snowflake] secrets, or None (no secrets file is normal)."""
    38|    try:
    39|        return dict(st.secrets["snowflake"]) if "snowflake" in st.secrets else None
    40|    except Exception:  # no secrets.toml at all: local or Streamlit in Snowflake
    41|        return None
    42|
    43|
    44|def _secrets_session(cfg: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
    45|    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
    46|    from snowflake.snowpark import Session
    47|
    48|    key = serialization.load_pem_private_key(cfg.pop("private_key_pem").encode(), password=None)
    49|    cfg["private_key"] = key.private_bytes(
    50|        serialization.Encoding.DER,
    51|        serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,
    52|        serialization.NoEncryption(),
    53|    )
    54|    cfg["authenticator"] = "SNOWFLAKE_JWT"
    55|    cfg.setdefault("application", "risk_copilot_app")
    56|    return Session.builder.configs(cfg).create()
    57|
    58|
    59|@st.cache_resource(show_spinner=False)
    60|def session() -> Any:
    61|    if (cfg := _secrets()) is not None:  # Streamlit Community Cloud
    62|        return _secrets_session(cfg)
    63|    try:
    64|        from risk_copilot.config import load_settings
    65|        from risk_copilot.session import create_session
    66|    except ImportError:  # Streamlit in Snowflake
    67|        return st.connection("snowflake").session()
    68|    return create_session(load_settings(), unattended=True)
    69|
    70|
    71|def query(sql: str, params: list[Any] | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    72|    """Run one statement; columns lower-cased."""
    73|    df = session().sql(sql, params=params or []).to_pandas()
    74|    df.columns = [c.lower() for c in df.columns]
    75|    return df
    76|
    77|

class _Sessions:
    """Stands in for the cached ``session()``: a new object after each clear."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.made = 0
        self.cleared = 0

    def __call__(self) -> int:
        self.made += 1
        return self.cleared

    def clear(self) -> None:
        self.cleared += 1

"""``riskcopilot refresh`` -- every deployed dynamic table, at one data timestamp.

The operator's refresh during a live demo. ``verify`` refreshes only the signal
tables and what is upstream of them, so a table the app reads that is not
upstream of a signal (TXN_DAILY_AGG: the cash-deposit counts) kept its old rows
for the whole rehearsal (build log M48). One ``ALTER DYNAMIC TABLE a, b, ...
REFRESH`` refreshes them all, and their upstream tables, as one pipeline.

Only configured tables that are deployed are refreshed: a configured but unbuilt
table is skipped, and nothing outside ``dynamic_tables`` is touched.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

from risk_copilot.config import Settings, validate_identifier
from risk_copilot.session import execute


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Refreshed:
    name: str
    statistics: str


def targets(settings: Settings, live: set[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Fully qualified names of the configured dynamic tables that are deployed, sorted."""
    schema = settings.fq("curated")
    names = {settings.obj(spec.name) for spec in settings.dynamic_tables.values()}
    return [
        f"{schema}.{validate_identifier(n, what='Dynamic table name')}"
        for n in sorted(names & {n.upper() for n in live})
    ]


def refresh_all(settings: Settings, session: Any) -> list[Refreshed]:
    """Refresh every deployed dynamic table in one statement. Cannot run in a transaction."""
    live = {str(r["name"]) for r in execute(session, f"SHOW DYNAMIC TABLES IN SCHEMA {settings.fq('curated')}")}
    tables = targets(settings, live)
    if not tables:
        return []
    rows = execute(session, f"ALTER DYNAMIC TABLE {', '.join(tables)} REFRESH")
    return [Refreshed(str(r[0]), str(r[1])) for r in rows]

"""``riskcopilot refresh``: which dynamic tables it refreshes, offline."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest

from risk_copilot.config import load_settings
from risk_copilot.pipeline.refresh import refresh_all, targets

pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit


@pytest.fixture
def settings(repo_root: Path):  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
    return load_settings(repo_root=repo_root, profile="dev")


def test_only_deployed_configured_tables(settings) -> None:  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
    schema = settings.fq("curated")
    signals = settings.obj(settings.dt("signals_fast").name)
    daily = settings.obj(settings.dt("txn_daily_agg").name)
    live = {signals, daily.lower(), "SOMEONE_ELSES_DT"}
    assert targets(settings, live) == sorted([f"{schema}.{signals}", f"{schema}.{daily}"])


def test_nothing_deployed_refreshes_nothing(settings) -> None:  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
    class Session:
        def __init__(self) -> None:
            self.sql: list[str] = []

        def sql_rows(self, sql: str) -> list[Any]:
            self.sql.append(sql)
            return []

    s = Session()
    import risk_copilot.pipeline.refresh as module

    original = module.execute
    module.execute = lambda session, sql, params=None: session.sql_rows(sql)  # type: ignore[assignment]
    try:
        assert refresh_all(settings, s) == []
    finally:
        module.execute = original
    assert len(s.sql) == 1 and s.sql[0].startswith("SHOW DYNAMIC TABLES")


def test_one_statement_refreshes_them_all(settings, monkeypatch) -> None:  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
    import risk_copilot.pipeline.refresh as module

    seen: list[str] = []
    live = [{"name": settings.obj(spec.name)} for spec in settings.dynamic_tables.values()][:3]

    def fake(session: Any, sql: str, params: Any = None) -> list[Any]:
        seen.append(sql)
        if sql.startswith("SHOW"):
            return live
        return [(t, "No new data") for t in sql.split("TABLE ", 1)[1].split(" REFRESH")[0].split(", ")]

    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "execute", fake)
    done = refresh_all(settings, object())
    assert len(seen) == 2 and seen[1].startswith("ALTER DYNAMIC TABLE ") and seen[1].endswith(" REFRESH")
    assert len(done) == 3
